chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man appoints another man as executor of his will while he (the latter) is absent, then it is not for him to repudiate (turn down) his appointment. But if he appoints him and he is in the city, then he has the choice: if he wishes he accepts, and if he does not wish he does not accept.

key_terms.الخيار: Khiyar — option/right of choice, a key concept in Islamic contract and estate law
key_terms.وصيّة: Wasiyyah — testamentary bequest or appointment of an executor
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Wasi — executor or trustee of a will

ai.seo_question: Can an absent person reject being named executor of a will in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) established a key rule of wasiyyah (testamentary executorship): an absent designee cannot reject the appointment after the fact, but one who is present in the same city retains the right to decline when informed. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that obligations arising from absence differ from those where knowledge and acceptance are contemporaneous with the appointment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hamaad Bin Isa, from Rabie, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If a man appoints a man as an executor (of his will) and he is absent, so it is not for him that he should repudiate (turn down) his appointment. So if he appoints him and he is in the city, so he is with the choice, if he likes he accepts, and if he (does not) like he does not accept’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘iy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “

If one makes a will and appoints a certain person as the executor of the will who is not present in town he cannot refuse to accept the appointment, but if he is town he has the choice to accept or refuse it.’”
